The dvojnice (diple) is a traditional wooden wind instrument from the Adriatic coast, an aerophone, H-S number 422.12. It is built as a single body containing two bores and fitted with two separate single reeds, so that it can sound a melody and a harmony at once. The left hand covers the group of holes on the left and the right hand the group on the right; the bag version is fed air through a blowpipe, and the bag is usually of goatskin. It is used in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Slovenia, Montenegro and Serbia, and the tuning and ornaments differ from place to place, the intonation varying by region.

在亞得里亞海沿岸與巴爾幹地區的傳統音樂中出現，見於克羅埃西亞、斯洛維尼亞、波士尼: It appears in the traditional music of the Adriatic coast and the Balkans, in the traditional playing of Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Serbia. The bag form sounds melody and harmony together on two chanters and uses no drone pipe; its area runs from Istria through Lika and Dalmatia and southwards, and the tuning, ornament and fine detail of playing differ from place to place.
演奏雙管笛時，左手按管身左側一組音孔，右手按另一側；樂器有兩個管膛，可同時發出兩: To play the dvojnice, the left hand covers one group of fingerholes on the side of the body and the right hand the other side; the instrument has two bores and can sound two notes at once. In the bag form the player blows air through the blowpipe into a leather bag and it sounds through the two single reeds on the twin chanters; there is no drone pipe, and melody and harmony are both played on the chanters. A beginner should first master the division between the hands and covering the holes at the same time, then practise a steady supply of air so that both bores sound together; the tuning and ornaments differ from place to place, and must be adjusted to the region being learnt.

Unlike most European bagpipes it has no drone pipe, and the harmony is played on the twin chanter itself. Its intonation is not equal-tempered, and differences of tuning, ornament and detail from place to place give the sound a regional character.

雙管笛（Diple）起源於亞得里亞海沿岸，屬木管簧樂器，以單一器身設兩個管孔，同: The diple comes from the Adriatic coast; it is a reed woodwind with two bores in a single body, sounding two notes at once. Its bagpipe form comes from the coastal regions of Dalmatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro, and spread from Istria through Lika, Dalmatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina to Montenegro. Unlike most European bagpipes it has no drone pipe, playing melody and harmony together on twin chanters; tuning, ornaments and intonation differ from place to place, and it is not an equal-tempered instrument.
